hints: Calculate the change in kinetic energy using $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2)$ with $m = 800\text{ kg}$, $u = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $v = 14\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find the vertical height gained as $h = d\sin\theta = 120 \times 0.15$.
Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy using $\Delta E_p = mgh = 800 \times 10 \times h$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for change in kinetic energy:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2)$$

Substitute the mass $m = 800\text{ kg}$, initial speed $u = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and final speed $v = 14\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 800 \times (14^2 - 8^2)$$

Calculate the squared speeds and their difference:
$$14^2 = 196, \quad 8^2 = 64 \implies 196 - 64 = 132$$
$$\Delta E_k = 400 \times 132 = 52800\text{ J}$$

State the formula for change in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh$$

Calculate the vertical height $h$ gained along the inclined slope of length $d = 120\text{ m}$:
$$h = d\sin\theta = 120 \times 0.15 = 18\text{ m}$$

Substitute mass $m = 800\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h = 18\text{ m}$ into the potential energy formula:
$$\Delta E_p = 800 \times 10 \times 18 = 8000 \times 18 = 144000\text{ J}$$

hints: Calculate total work input from the engine using $W = P \times t$, converting $32\text{ kW}$ to $32000\text{ W}$ over $t = 12\text{ s}$.
Set up the work-energy balance: the total work supplied by the engine equals the gain in kinetic energy plus the gain in potential energy plus the work done against resistance.
Substitute $\Delta E_k = 52800\text{ J}$ and $\Delta E_p = 144000\text{ J}$ from part (i) into $W_{\text{engine}} = \Delta E_k + \Delta E_p + W_{\text{res}}$ and solve for $W_{\text{res}}$.
walkthrough:
State the formula relating energy (work done) to constant power and time:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = P \times t$$

Convert the engine power from kilowatts to watts:
$$P = 32\text{ kW} = 32 \times 1000 = 32000\text{ W}$$

Substitute power $P = 32000\text{ W}$ and time $t = 12\text{ s}$ to find the total work done by the engine:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = 32000 \times 12 = 384000\text{ J}$$

State the work-energy principle relating work input to mechanical energy gains and resistance work:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = \Delta E_k + \Delta E_p + W_{\text{res}}$$

Substitute the kinetic energy gain ($52800\text{ J}$) and potential energy gain ($144000\text{ J}$) found in part (i):
$$384000 = 52800 + 144000 + W_{\text{res}}$$

Sum the two mechanical energy gains:
$$52800 + 144000 = 196800\text{ J}$$
$$384000 = 196800 + W_{\text{res}}$$

Subtract $196800$ from both sides to find $W_{\text{res}}$:
$$W_{\text{res}} = 384000 - 196800 = 187200\text{ J}$$
